Graded take-home exercises for **ISSS626: Geospatial Analytics and Applications**
at Singapore Management University. Each one is a self-contained analysis with its
own data pipeline, technical report and executive summary.

::: {.coursework-group}

::: {.coursework-group-header}
<span class="coursework-number">01</span>
<span class="coursework-group-title">Take-home Exercise 1</span>
:::

<p class="coursework-group-desc">Point-pattern analysis of NASA FIRMS VIIRS
active-fire detections in Pulang Pisau Regency, Central Kalimantan, across the 2026
dry season. The analysis argues that a satellite hotspot is not a fire, replaces
complete spatial randomness with an inhomogeneous Poisson null, and tests
space-time interaction by random labelling with <code>spatstat</code>.</p>

[<span class="exercise-row-label">Report</span><span class="exercise-row-title">Geospatial Analytics for Public Safety</span><span class="exercise-row-arrow">→</span>](Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex01/index.qmd){.exercise-row}

:::

::: {.coursework-group-header}
<span class="coursework-number">02</span>
<span class="coursework-group-title">Take-home Exercise 2</span>
:::

<p class="coursework-group-desc">Local spatial association and emerging hot spots
of armed conflict across Myanmar's 330 townships, January 2021 to September 2025,
from ACLED political-violence events. Local Moran's I and Gi* locate the clusters,
Mann-Kendall and EHSA follow them through 19 quarters, and a spatial Markov chain
tests whether violence spreads from a township to its neighbours.</p>

[<span class="exercise-row-label">Report</span><span class="exercise-row-title">Geospatial Analytics for Peace</span><span class="exercise-row-arrow">→</span>](Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex02/index.qmd){.exercise-row}
